## This is the ninth (and last) bugfix release of Python 3.11

Python 3.11.9 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations.

## Major new features of the 3.11 series, compared to 3.10

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.11 are:

## General changes

*   [PEP 657](link_1) -- Include Fine-Grained Error Locations in Tracebacks
*   [PEP 654](link_2) -- Exception Groups and `except*`
*   [PEP 680](link_3) -- tomllib: Support for Parsing TOML in the Standard Library
*   [gh-90908](link_5) -- Introduce task groups to asyncio
*   [gh-34627](link_6) -- Atomic grouping (`(?>...)`) and possessive quantifiers (`*+, ++, ?+, {m,n}+`) are now supported in regular expressions. 
*   The [Faster CPython Project](link_7) is already yielding some exciting results. Python 3.11 is up to 10-60% faster than Python 3.10. On average, we measured a 1.22x speedup on the standard benchmark suite. See [Faster CPython](link_9) for details.

## Typing and typing language changes

*   [PEP 673](link_10) -- Self Type
*   [PEP 646](link_11) -- Variadic Generics
*   [PEP 675](link_12) -- Arbitrary Literal String Type
*   [PEP 655](link_13) -- Marking individual TypedDict items as required or potentially-missing
*   [PEP 681](link_14) -- Data Class Transforms

## More resources

*   [Online Documentation](link_8)
*   [PEP 664](link_15), 3.11 Release Schedule
*   Report bugs at [https://github.com/python/cpython/issues](link_4).
*   [Help fund Python and its community](link_16).

## And now for something completely different

A kugelblitz is a theoretical astrophysical object predicted by general relativity. It is a concentration of heat, light or radiation so intense that its energy forms an event horizon and becomes self-trapped. In other words, if enough radiation is aimed into a region of space, the concentration of energy can warp spacetime so much that it creates a black hole. This would be a black hole whose original mass–energy was in the form of radiant energy rather than matter, however as soon as it forms, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary black hole.

## This is the ninth (and last) bugfix release of Python 3.11

Python 3.11.9 is the newest major release of the Python programming language, and it contains many new features and optimizations.

## Major new features of the 3.11 series, compared to 3.10

Some of the new major new features and changes in Python 3.11 are:

## General changes

*   [PEP 657](link_1) -- Include Fine-Grained Error Locations in Tracebacks
*   [PEP 654](link_2) -- Exception Groups and `except*`
*   [PEP 680](link_3) -- tomllib: Support for Parsing TOML in the Standard Library
*   [gh-90908](link_5) -- Introduce task groups to asyncio
*   [gh-34627](link_6) -- Atomic grouping (`(?>...)`) and possessive quantifiers (`*+, ++, ?+, {m,n}+`) are now supported in regular expressions. 
*   The [Faster CPython Project](link_7) is already yielding some exciting results. Python 3.11 is up to 10-60% faster than Python 3.10. On average, we measured a 1.22x speedup on the standard benchmark suite. See [Faster CPython](link_9) for details.

## Typing and typing language changes

*   [PEP 673](link_10) -- Self Type
*   [PEP 646](link_11) -- Variadic Generics
*   [PEP 675](link_12) -- Arbitrary Literal String Type
*   [PEP 655](link_13) -- Marking individual TypedDict items as required or potentially-missing
*   [PEP 681](link_14) -- Data Class Transforms

## More resources

*   [Online Documentation](link_8)
*   [PEP 664](link_15), 3.11 Release Schedule
*   Report bugs at [https://github.com/python/cpython/issues](link_4).
*   [Help fund Python and its community](link_16).

## And now for something completely different

A kugelblitz is a theoretical astrophysical object predicted by general relativity. It is a concentration of heat, light or radiation so intense that its energy forms an event horizon and becomes self-trapped. In other words, if enough radiation is aimed into a region of space, the concentration of energy can warp spacetime so much that it creates a black hole. This would be a black hole whose original mass–energy was in the form of radiant energy rather than matter, however as soon as it forms, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary black hole.

*   [gh-34627](link_6) -- Atomic grouping (`(?>...)`) and possessive quantifiers (`*+, ++, ?+, {m,n}+`) are now supported in regular expressions. 
*   The [Faster CPython Project](link_7) is already yielding some exciting results. Python 3.11 is up to 10-60% faster than Python 3.10. On average, we measured a 1.22x speedup on the standard benchmark suite. See [Faster CPython](link_9) for details.

*   [PEP 673](link_10) -- Self Type

*   Report bugs at [https://github.com/python/cpython/issues](link_4).
*   [Help fund Python and its community](link_16).

## And now for something completely different

A kugelblitz is a theoretical astrophysical object predicted by general relativity. It is a concentration of heat, light or radiation so intense that its energy forms an event horizon and becomes self-trapped. In other words, if enough radiation is aimed into a region of space, the concentration of energy can warp spacetime so much that it creates a black hole. This would be a black hole whose original mass–energy was in the form of radiant energy rather than matter, however as soon as it forms, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary black hole.
